title: Canonical data and map words for finite scalar mate realization
statement: Fix the finite-field datum, prime, coefficient extension and separated finite-type morphism with compactification of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. On the small pro-etale sites use the completed integral constructible categories and strict-tower scalar functor of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. Define a finite-scalar-mate context to consist of simultaneous derived-system calculi at E and L on X, the compactification and Y, their specified normalized finite exceptional realizations and integral compact-support realizations [def-coef-adjunction-evaluation, lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus, lem-coef-finite-adjunction-diagram-realization, def-coef-finite-adjunction-system-data], preservation proofs for reduction, scalar extension and completed scalar extension, integral right adjoints with adjunctions to the fixed integral compact-support functors, and their cochain-normalized scalar realization comparisons [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint, def-sf-integral-comparison-system-data, def-trf-integral-comparison-realization-models]. The context imposes no equality of maps; the comparison equations are asserted by the finite-scalar-mate theorem. Restrict the canonical sequence-site scalar functor and its proper/open comparison [def-weil-system-operation-exchange-realization] to these full subcategories. Define alpha by the canonical adjoint-uniqueness support presentations and the proper scalar mate followed by the open tensor comparison, and, when alpha is invertible, beta to be its inverse's adjunction mate. These are actual natural transformations before evaluation. For e positive with pi S=v^e S, use the arithmetic index r(n)=e(n+1)-1 of [def-sp-strict-tower-arithmetic-restriction-data], the ramified quotient inclusion and canonical proper/open scalar comparison of [lem-pur-compact-support-integral-coefficient-comparison, def-pur-finite-compact-support-scalar-data]. Thus r(n)+1=e(n+1), r is monotone, and the actual scalar/quotient square commutes; its tensor square is the unit-normalized tensor-composition comparison. Define the retained restriction by exact arithmetic restriction of the entire strict completed-coefficient tower, and its total derived limit using the published total-limit functor on the completed-coefficient module categories [def-sf-scalar-reduction-categories-restriction]. The full and retained Roos comparison maps are induced by the exact-localization factors followed by the published normalized Roos comparisons [def-sf-strict-roos-functor]. The integral alpha component is the canonical completed proper/open scalar map, conjugated by the prescribed completion comparison [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] and compact-support realization. Finite scalar restriction uses the unchanged ambient derived tensor and the finite-Tor subcategory inclusions of [lem-coef-finite-exceptional, lem-coef-finite-free-extension].
